title: Freight broker payment delays: managing accounts receivable on your Mac
metaTitle: Solving Freight Broker Payment Delays: AR Management on Mac
description: Stop freight broker payment delays by mastering your accounts receivable process. Learn how to fix billing errors and improve cash flow on your Mac.
intro: Freight broker payment delays often stem from incomplete documentation and manual billing errors that stall the entire collection cycle. By shifting from reactive manual entry to proactive, automated workflows, you can resolve these bottlenecks and secure your thin net margins.
tldr: Freight brokerages operate on thin margins, meaning one unpaid invoice can wipe out profits from dozens of loads.
Most payment delays are caused by missing proof of delivery or rate confirmation mismatches.
Only 2% of brokerages have fully automated their accounts receivable process.
You can reduce processing costs from over $12 to under $3 per invoice using better tools.
Use browser-native platforms on your Mac to avoid the performance issues of legacy Windows software.

blocks.text: Why freight broker payment delays happen

The primary cause of payment delays is a disconnect between your operational data and your billing cycle. When you rely on manual entry, small mistakes like a missing digit in a zip code or an incomplete proof of delivery stop your invoice from being processed. Shippers often have strict requirements. If your paperwork is incomplete, they will not pay until you provide the correct files. This creates a cash gap where you have already paid your carriers, but your revenue remains stuck in limbo.
The cost of manual accounts receivable management

Manual management is expensive. Between the time spent chasing documents and the cost of resolving errors, your profit margin shrinks. Every hour you spend re-keying data from an email into your TMS is an hour you are not finding new capacity or closing a high-margin load. When you account for the $53.50 average cost to fix a single billing error, it becomes clear that manual processes are a major drain on your bottom line.

items: Enforce a strict no-bill-without-complete-paperwork policy in your TMS to ensure every invoice is ready before it is sent.
Use automated dunning tools to send payment reminders based on a set schedule instead of relying on human memory.
Connect your TMS directly to your accounting software like QuickBooks Online to eliminate manual data exports.
Flag potential disputes early by tracking short-pays as soon as they appear in your ledger.

blocks.text: Choosing the right tools for your Mac

When you work on a Mac, you should prioritize tools that run directly in your browser. Legacy software that requires Java wrappers or remote desktop apps like Citrix often causes performance lag. Look for cloud-native platforms like Tailwind TMS or Tai TMS. These tools work in Chrome or Safari without the need for complex installations. By using browser-native apps, you keep your workflow fast and avoid the dreaded spinning beachball.

faq.question: Why does my freight software run slowly on my Mac?
faq.answer: If you are using legacy Windows-based software through a remote desktop connection or a Java wrapper, it will likely be slow. Switch to browser-native, cloud-based TMS platforms to improve performance.

faq.question: How can I reduce billing errors in my brokerage?
faq.answer: Automate your data entry by linking your TMS directly to your accounting software. This removes the manual step of re-keying information, which is where most errors occur.
